newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cuts coffee output forecast, raises price.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cuts coffee output forecast, raises price.

text.p: The veteran chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation cut his forecast for output in the 1996/97 coffee year to 11 million 60-kg bags on Monday and said the federation would be forced to draw on domestic stockpiles to meet its commitments abroad.

Federation leader Jorge Cardenas announced his revised forecast for production during the current coffee year after a weekly policy meeting in which Colombia's internal coffee price was raised nearly 17 percent, to 290,000 pesos per 60-kilo bag, in a bid to bring it closer to world market prices.

Cardenas, who spoke at an impromptu news conference, gave no specific reason other than the climate for his lower estimate of coffee production during the current coffee year, but industry sources have said that unusually heavy rains during last month's flowering period had adversely affected the 1996/97 crop.
Cardenas' previous estimate was for production of about 11.6 million 60-kg bags, down from 12.9 million in the 1995/96 coffee year.
He stressed that Colombia had 6 million 60-kilo bags in inventories, however, and said the country would have no problem meeting its commitments for delivery to roasters abroad.
Colombia's internal coffee price was raised to 248,125 pesos per 125-kg load on Jan. 31, but the hike fell short of growers' hopes in light of a run-up in prices in New York and London.
To bring it closer in line with overseas prices, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said the new price, effective immediately, had been set at a record-high 290,000 pesos.
Ocampo, who participated in the weekly meeting at federation headquarters, also said the price would be revised on a weekly basis and increased if world prices continue to trend upwards.
If world prices go down, Ocampo said the government and National Coffee Fund would guarantee growers a minimum price of of 221,500 pesos per 125-kg load.
If Colombian excelso fetches an average of about $1.45 this year, Ocampo estimated national coffee income at $2 billion.
"This is a relief for coffee growers," Cardenas said of the nearly 17 percent increase in Colombia's internal price." They (growers) have had to put up with bad prices for many years now."
